The stipulator himself, but not his creditors or heirs, may revoke the stipulation for a third party, provided that the revocation is made before the beneficiary advises the debtor or the stipulator of his wish to have the benefit of the stipulation, and that the revocation is not contrary to the spirit of the contract. [EN] State Article 962 of the Egyptian Civil Code verbatim.

A person who remains in possession of an immovable for a whole year may, if he has good grounds to fear disturbance as a result of new works which threaten his possession, apply to the Judge to order the suspension of such works, provided that they have not been finished and that a year has not elapsed since the commencement of the works which may cause him damage. The Judge may either stop or authorize the continuance of the works. In both cases he may order the provision of an adequate guarantee: in the case of a judgment ordering the suspension of the works, to cover compensation for damage caused by the suspension if a final decision shows that the claim for discontinuance of the works was without foundation; and in the case of a judgment ordering the continuance of the works, to cover the cost of their total or partial demolition as compensation for the damage suffered by the possessor if he obtains a final judgment in his favor.

A neighbor is not entitled to have a direct view over his neighbor at a distance of less than one meter.

### Text
A neighbor is not entitled to have a direct view over his neighbor at a distance of less than one meter. This distance is measured from the outside face of the wall in which the opening is made or from the outside line of the balcony or other projection. ### Topic
The Effects of a Mandate

### Key point
The mandatary is bound to perform the mandate without exceeding the limits fixed therein.

### Text
The mandatary is bound to perform the mandate without exceeding the limits fixed therein. He may, however, exceed these limits if he finds himself unable to notify the mandator thereof beforehand and if the circumstances are such that it can be assumed that the mandator could not have failed to approve the act. Gaming and Betting

### Text
When a contract provides that the worker will be entitled in addition to or in lieu of the agreed salary, to a share of the master's profits or to a percentage of the gross receipts or of the amount of production or of the value of the savings effected, or to other remuneration of alike nature, the master is bound to render to the worker, after each balance sheet, an account of the amount payable to him in this respect. ### Article Number
665

### Topic
Contracts for work

### Key point
When works are destroyed by a fortuitous event, before delivery to the master, the contractor has no claim either for the price of his work, or for reimbursement of his expenses.

### Text
When works are destroyed by a fortuitous event, before delivery to the master, the contractor has no claim either for the price of his work, or for reimbursement of his expenses. The loss of materials falls on the party who supplied them. When, however, the contractor fails to comply with a formal summons to deliver the work or when the works are destroyed or deteriorate before the delivery by the fault of the contractor, he is under a liability to indemnify the master for the materials supplied to carry out the works. When a master is formally summoned to take delivery of the works or when the works are destroyed or deteriorate by the fault of the master or by reason of a defect in the materials supplied by him, the master shall bear the loss resulting from the destruction of the materials and is liable to the contractor for his remuneration in addition to such compensation as may be due.

English:
A debtor who has made a tender of the debt followed by a deposit, or by an equivalent measure, may retract his tender as long as it has not been accepted by the creditor, or as long as it has not been recognized as valid by a final judgment, in which case the co-debtor and sureties will not be freed. If a debtor retracts his tender after its acceptance by the creditor or after it has been declared valid by a judgment, and his withdrawal is accepted by the creditor, the creditor shall no longer have the right, to avail himself of the securities guaranteeing his right, and the co-debtors and the sureties shall in such case be released.

### Text
If the third party who carried out the works mentioned in the preceding article honestly believed that he was entitled to do so, the owner of the land has no the right to demand their removal, but he may, at his option, and provided the third party does not claim their removal, pay the third party either the value of the materials and the cost of the work or a sum equal to the increased value that the works have given to the land. If, however, the works are so extensive that the payment of the amount due in respect thereof is onerous for the owner of the land, he may claim the conveyance of the ownership of the land to the third party against payment of an adequate compensation.

[EN] Show Article 536 of the Egyptian Civil Code as a structured card (number, topic, text).

### Article Number
536

### Topic
Liquidation and partition of the partnership property

### Key point
The partnership assets are divided between all partners after payment of creditors, deduction of amounts required to cover debts that have not fallen due or are subject to litigation and repayment of disbursements or loans that may have been made by one of the partners for the be […]

### Text
The partnership assets are divided between all partners after payment of creditors, deduction of amounts required to cover debts that have not fallen due or are subject to litigation and repayment of disbursements or loans that may have been made by one of the partners for the benefit of the partnership. Each partner shall take a sum equal to the value of his contribution to the capital of the partnership, as recorded in the partnership deed, or, if not recorded in the partnership deed, at its value at the time the contribution was brought to the partnership, unless he has only contributed his services, the usufruct or the mere use of the thing that he has brought to the partnership. The balance, if any, will be distributed between the partners proportionally to each partner's share in the profits. If the partnership assets are not sufficient to cover the repayment of the partners’ contributions, the loss is shared between the partner’s proportionally to each partner's share in the losses.

[EN] Give a reference card for Article 1128 of the Egyptian Civil Code: the article number, the topic it falls under, and its text.

### Article Number
1128

### Topic
Pledge of Debts

### Key point
If a pledged debt falls due for payment before the actual debt secured by the pledge, the debtor must discharge his debt to the pledgee and the pledgor jointly.

### Text
If a pledged debt falls due for payment before the actual debt secured by the pledge, the debtor must discharge his debt to the pledgee and the pledgor jointly. The pledgee and the pledgor may each demand the debtor to deposit the amount paid by him, in which case the pledge is transferred to the amount so deposited. The pledgee and the pledgor must, without prejudice to the rights of the secured creditors, cooperate together for the investment of the amount paid by the debtor to the best advantage of the pledgor, and they must immediately constitute a new pledge in favor of the pledgee.

### Article Number
815

### Topic
Restrictions on the Right of Ownership

### Key point
An owner may, if he has good reason to do so, heighten a party wall, provided that he does not thereby cause serious prejudice to his co-owner.

### Text
An owner may, if he has good reason to do so, heighten a party wall, provided that he does not thereby cause serious prejudice to his co-owner. He must alone bear the cost of heightening as well as of the maintenance of the part so heightened and carry out the necessary work, so that the wall may support the extra weight due to the heightening without its strength being diminished. If the party wall is not able to support the heightening, the co-owner who desires to heighten the wall must reconstruct the wall entirely at his own cost, in such a way as the thickening shall, as far as possible, abut on his side. The reconstructed wall remains, apart from the heightened parts, a party wall, but the neighbors who has re-heightened the wall cannot claim compensation whatever.

### Text
When payment is made by a third party, such third party is subrogated in the rights of the creditor who is paid off in the following cases: a) when such third party was liable for the debt jointly with the debtor or was under an obligation to pay the debt on his behalf; b) when such third party, being himself a creditor, even an unsecured creditor, had paid another creditor ranking before him by reason of a real security; c) when, having acquired an immovable, he has paid the price to creditors having a real security upon the immovable in question; d) when the law expressly gives him the right of subrogation.

The End of Contracts of Service

### Text
A contract of service is not dissolved by the death of the master, unless the personality of the master was a factor taken into consideration in concluding the contract. The contract however, is dissolved by the death of the worker. The rules laid down in special laws on the subject will be observed for the dissolution of the contract on account of the death or prolonged illness of the worker or of any other cause constituting force majeure which prevents the worker from continuing his work.

### Article Number
270

### Topic
Conditional Obligations

### Key point
The fulfillment of a condition is effective retroactively to the day on which the obligation was contracted unless it appears from the will of the parties or by reason of the nature of the contract that the existence of the obligation or its extinction should take effect from the […]

### Text
The fulfillment of a condition is effective retroactively to the day on which the obligation was contracted unless it appears from the will of the parties or by reason of the nature of the contract that the existence of the obligation or its extinction should take effect from the moment of the fulfillment of the condition. In any case, the condition will not have retroactive effect if the execution of the obligation becomes impossible before the fulfillment of the condition, on account of a cause independent of the debtor and for which he is not responsible.

He has also the right to collect periodical payments appertaining to the pledged debt upon condition that he sets off the amounts so collected by him first against expenses, then against the interest and then against the capital of the debt secured by the pledge. [EN] Show Article 708 of the Egyptian Civil Code as a structured card (number, topic, text).

### Article Number
708

### Topic
The Effects of a Mandate

### Key point
A mandatary who nominates a substitute to perform his mandate without being authorized to do so, is responsible for the acts of the substitute as if they were his own acts: in such a case, the mandatary and his substitute are jointly and severally responsible.

### Text
A mandatary who nominates a substitute to perform his mandate without being authorized to do so, is responsible for the acts of the substitute as if they were his own acts: in such a case, the mandatary and his substitute are jointly and severally responsible. When a mandatary is authorized to appoint a substitute without specifying the person, he is only liable for a faulty choice of the substitute or for faulty instructions that he gives to him. In the two preceding cases, the mandator and the substitute of the mandatary have a direct right of action against each other.

[EN] State Article 1144 of the Egyptian Civil Code verbatim.

Sums due to hotel proprietors by a traveller for accommodation, food and expenses incurred for his account, are secured by a privilege over the effects brought by the traveller to the hotel or its annexes. Unless it can be shown that the hotel proprietor knew of the existence of a third party's rights over these effects at the time they were brought on to the premises, this privilege may be enforced on these effects, even if they do not belong to the traveller, provided that they are not lost or stolen property. An hotel proprietor may, if he has not been paid in full, object to the removal of these effects, and if they are removed notwithstanding his objection or without his knowledge, the privilege continues to be enforceable on them, subject to the rights acquired by third parties in good faith. An hotel proprietor's privilege has the same rank as a lessor's privilege. Should the effects in question be subject to both claims, the first in date will have priority, unless it is not enforceable against the other.

[EN] Give me the English text of Article 1039 of the Egyptian Civil Code.

A mortgage granted by all the co-owners of an immovable held in common remains effective whatever may be the ultimate result of a partition of the immovable or if its sale by auction owing to impossibility of partition. If one of the owners grants a mortgage on his undivided share or on a divided part of an immovable and, as a result of the partition, a property other than the mortgaged property is attributed to him, the mortgage will be transferred, with its degree of priority, to a portion of this property equivalent in value to the value of the property formerly mortgaged. This portion will, upon petition, be fixed by an order of the Judge. The mortgagee shall be bound, within ninety days of the notification of the transcription of the partition made to him by any interested party, to proceed with a new inscription describing the portion of the property to which the mortgage has been transferred. The mortgage so transferred shall not have any prejudicial effect on a mortgage already granted by all the co-owners or on the privileges of co-partitioners.

[EN] Summarise where Article 828 of the Egyptian Civil Code belongs and what it says, as a labelled card.

### Article Number
828

### Topic
Provisions Relating to Joint Ownership

### Key point
A decision taken by the majority of the co-owners as to ordinary acts of management is binding on all of them.

### Text
A decision taken by the majority of the co-owners as to ordinary acts of management is binding on all of them. The majority shall be calculated on the basis of the value of their shares. Failing a majority, the Court may, upon the application of any one of the co-owners, take such measures as may be necessary in the circumstances and appoint, if needs be, a manager to manage the property owned in common. The majority may select a manager and may also establish rules for the management and fuller enjoyment of the property owned in common, which rules shall also be binding upon the successors in title of all the co- owners whether such successors in title are universal or particular. A co-owner who conducts the management of the joint property, without any objection being raised by the other co-owners, is considered to be their mandatory.

### Text
The provisions of this Section as to contracts of service apply to the relationship between masters and canvassers, commercial representatives, commercial travellers, assurance agents and other intermediaries, even if they remunerated on a commission basis or if they work for the account of several employers at the same time, so long as these persons work under the orders and supervision of such masters. When the services of a commercial representative or a commercial traveller comes to an end, even by reason of the expiration of the term of employment specified in the contract, he shall not be entitled to receive, by way of remuneration, the commission or discount, agreed upon or established by custom, or orders which do not reach the master until after the commercial representative or the - 109 - traveller has left his service, if such orders are the direct result of the employee's representations (demarches) to customers while he was in the master's service. Such employees, however, can only claim this right during the usual period for such claims established by custom in respect of each business.

If the debtor has given real securities in guarantee of the original obligation, the following conditions will be observed in the agreement providing for the transfer of these securities to the new obligation: a) when the novation results from a change of the debt, the creditor and the debtor may agree that the securities shall be transferred to the new obligation, to the extent that such a transfer does not cause prejudice to third parties; b) when the novation results from a change of the debtor, the creditor and the new debtor may agree, without the consent of the original debtor, that the real securities shall be maintained; c) when the novation results from a change of the creditor, the three contracting parties may agree that the securities shall be maintained. 534

### Topic
Liquidation and partition of the partnership property

### Key point
The liquidation will be carried out either by all the partners of by one or more liquidators appointed by the majority of the partners, as the case may be.

### Text
The liquidation will be carried out either by all the partners of by one or more liquidators appointed by the majority of the partners, as the case may be. If the partners do not agree on the appointment of a liquidator, such liquidator will, upon the application of one of the partners, be appointed by the judge. In case of nullity of partnership, the Court will appoint a liquidator and will decided upon the method of liquidation upon the application of any interested party. Until a liquidator is appointed, the managing partners shall be deemed, as far as third parties are concerned, to be the liquidators.

A debtor who has made a tender of the debt followed by a deposit, or by an equivalent measure, may retract his tender as long as it has not been accepted by the creditor, or as long as it has not been recognized as valid by a final judgment, in which case the co-debtor and sureties will not be freed. ### Text
If, after the lease has expired, the lessee continues to enjoy the leased property to the knowledge of and without objection on the part of the lessor, the lessee is deemed to be renewed upon the same conditions but for an indefinite duration. The lease so renewed is governed by the provisions of Article 563. The tacit renewal is deemed to be a new lease and not a mere prolongation of the original lease. Nevertheless, subject to the rules of publication applicable to real property, the real securities supplied by the lessee in guarantee of the old lease are transferred to the new lease. The suretyship, whether personal or real, is not transferred to the new lease unless the surety consents thereto.

A state of insolvency ceases by virtue of a judgment of the Court of First Instance in the district in which the domicile of the debtor is situated, delivered upon application of any interested party in the two following cases: a) if it is established that the liabilities of the debtor are no longer in excess of his assets; b) if the debtor effects payment of the debts that were due by him as apart from those that became due as a result of the declaration of insolvency. In such a case, debts that became due as a result of the insolvency become, in accordance with Article 263, once again payable on the dates upon which they were due before the declaration of insolvency. It is the duty of the greffier of the court to record the judgment that puts an end to the state of insolvency in the margin of the registration provided for in Article 253. [EN] Summarise where Article 764 of the Egyptian Civil Code belongs and what it says, as a labelled card.

### Article Number
764

### Topic
Life Insurance

### Key point
Neither incorrect particulars nor misstatements as to the age of the life assured shall render the assurance void, unless the true age of the life assured exceeds the limit specified in the table of rates.

### Text
Neither incorrect particulars nor misstatements as to the age of the life assured shall render the assurance void, unless the true age of the life assured exceeds the limit specified in the table of rates. In all other cases, if, as a result of incorrect particulars or misstatements, the premium agreed upon is less than the premium which should have been paid, the sum assured shall be reduced in the proportion that the agreed premium bears to the premiums which should be paid on the basis of the true age. Should, however, the agreed premium be higher than the premium which should have been paid on the basis of the true age of the life assured the insurer shall be bound to refund, without interest, the excess received by him and to reduce the subsequent premiums to the limit corresponding to the true age of the life assured.

[EN] Summarise where Article 1048 of the Egyptian Civil Code belongs and what it says, as a labelled card.

### Article Number
1048

### Topic
Regards the Mortgagor

### Key point
If the mortgaged property perishes or deteriorates by the fault of the mortgagor, the mortgagee may either claim adequate security or immediate payment of the debt.

### Text
If the mortgaged property perishes or deteriorates by the fault of the mortgagor, the mortgagee may either claim adequate security or immediate payment of the debt. If the loss or deterioration is not imputable to the mortgagor and the mortgagee does not agree to leave his claim without security, the debtor may either furnish adequate security or pay the debt in full before it falls due. In the latter case, if the debt does not carry interest, the mortgagee has only a right to an amount equal to the amount of his claim less the interest calculated at the legal rate from the date of payment to the date of maturity. In all cases, if acts are done which may result in the loss of or deterioration to the mortgaged property, or which may render the mortgaged property insufficient to secure the debt, the mortgagee may apply to the Judge to order the cessation of such acts and the adoption of necessary measures to avoid the occurrence of the loss.

### Article Number
1113

### Topic
Extinguishment of a Pledge

### Key point
A right of pledge is also extinguished by one of the following causes: a- the renunciation of the right by the pledgee if he has the legal capacity to liberate the debtor of the debt.

### Text
A right of pledge is also extinguished by one of the following causes: a- the renunciation of the right by the pledgee if he has the legal capacity to liberate the debtor of the debt. The renunciation may result tacitly if the creditor voluntarily gives up the thing pledged or if he agrees without reserve to its alienation. If, however, the thing pledged is charged with a right in favor of a third party, the renunciation of the pledgee is only valid as regards such third party if such third party consents; b- the union of the right of pledge and that of ownership of the thing pledged in one and the same person; c- the loss of the thing pledged or the extinguishment of the right given in pledge.

### Text
A debtor has a right to compensation of that which he owes to his creditor against that which such creditor owes him, even when the causes giving rise to the two debts are different, provided that they are both for a sum of money or fungibles of a like nature and quality, that they are not in dispute and that they are due and may be sued for. Postponement of payment by reason of a delay granted by the Judge or by the creditor does not prevent compensation.

An owner may, if he has good reason to do so, heighten a party wall, provided that he does not thereby cause serious prejudice to his co-owner. He must alone bear the cost of heightening as well as of the maintenance of the part so heightened and carry out the necessary work, so that the wall may support the extra weight due to the heightening without its strength being diminished. If the party wall is not able to support the heightening, the co-owner who desires to heighten the wall must reconstruct the wall entirely at his own cost, in such a way as the thickening shall, as far as possible, abut on his side. The reconstructed wall remains, apart from the heightened parts, a party wall, but the neighbors who has re-heightened the wall cannot claim compensation whatever.

[EN] Complete Article 787 of the Egyptian Civil Code. It starts: "A creditor is bound to hand over to the surety, at the time of the discharge of the debt, all documents that are necessary to enable him to exercise his right of action. When a debt is secured by a pledge of an movable or by a right of retention on a movable, the creditor must …"

A creditor is bound to hand over to the surety, at the time of the discharge of the debt, all documents that are necessary to enable him to exercise his right of action. When a debt is secured by a pledge of an movable or by a right of retention on a movable, the creditor must surrender such securities to the surety. When, however, the debt is secured by a charge on an immovable property, the creditor must comply with the formalities required for the transfer of such security. The expenses of such transfer are borne by the surety, subject to his right of action against the debtor.

### Topic
Usufruct

Usufruct is extinguished by the loss of the property, but the usufruct is transmitted to any property obtained in lieu of the property destroyed.

### Text
Usufruct is extinguished by the loss of the property, but the usufruct is transmitted to any property obtained in lieu of the property destroyed. [EN] Show Article 154 of the Egyptian Civil Code as a structured card (number, topic, text).

### Article Number
154

### Topic
The Effects of a Contract

### Key point
A person may by a contract in his own name stipulate that an obligation shall be performed for the benefit of a third party, when he has a personal interest, material or moral, in the performance of such an obligation.

### Text
A person may by a contract in his own name stipulate that an obligation shall be performed for the benefit of a third party, when he has a personal interest, material or moral, in the performance of such an obligation. As a result of such a stipulation and in the absence of an agreement to the contrary, the third party beneficiary acquires a direct right against the person who undertook to perform the obligation, and may call upon him to do so. The person who gave the undertaking may set up against the beneficiary the defenses arising out of the contract. The stipulation may also demand the performance of the obligation in favor of the beneficiary, unless it appears from the contract that performance may only be demanded by the beneficiary.

The Effects of Mortgage as Regards Third Parties

### Topic

Subject to a clause or custom to the contrary, the price is payable at the time of delivery of the thing sold is made.

Subject to a clause or custom to the contrary, the price is payable at the time of delivery of the thing sold is made. ### Topic
One of the Means of Security the Right of Retention

### Key point

### Text
A person who is under an obligation to supply something, may refrain from performing his obligation so long as his creditor does not offer to perform an obligation incumbent on him arising out of the obligation of the debtor and connected therewith, or as long as the creditor does not supply adequate security to guarantee the performance of his obligation. This right belongs especially to the possessor or holder of a thing, if he has incurred expenditure of a necessary or useful kind on the thing. The possessor or holder may, in such a case, refuse to return the thing until he has been repaid the amount due to him, unless the obligation of restitution results from an unlawful act.

### Text
A special mandate, in respect of any act which is not an act of management, is required, and in particular for a sale, a mortgage, a gift, a compromise, an admission, an arbitration, the tendering of an oath and representation before the Courts. The administrator will discharge the debts of the estate with funds derived from claims recovered, cash in hand, proceeds of the sale of securities at market prices, proceeds of the sale of movables and, if the funds so obtained are insufficient, with the proceeds of the sale of immovable property of the estate. ### Text
A movable is deemed to have no owner when its owner abandons possession of it with the intention of renouncing his ownership thereto. Animals, other than domestic animals, are deemed to have no owner as long as they are at liberty. If one of such animals, after losing its liberty, regains its freedom, it becomes without an owner if the owner does not seek it immediately or ceases to seek for it. An animal that has become tame and is accustomed to return to the same place becomes again without an owner if it loses this habit.

[EN] Complete Article 665 of the Egyptian Civil Code. It starts: "When works are destroyed by a fortuitous event, before delivery to the master, the contractor has no claim either for the price of his work, or for reimbursement of his expenses. The loss of materials falls on the party who supplied them. When, however, the contractor fails to comply with a formal summons to deliver the work or when the works are destroyed or deteriorate before the delivery by the fault of the contractor, he is under …"

When works are destroyed by a fortuitous event, before delivery to the master, the contractor has no claim either for the price of his work, or for reimbursement of his expenses. The loss of materials falls on the party who supplied them. When, however, the contractor fails to comply with a formal summons to deliver the work or when the works are destroyed or deteriorate before the delivery by the fault of the contractor, he is under a liability to indemnify the master for the materials supplied to carry out the works. When a master is formally summoned to take delivery of the works or when the works are destroyed or deteriorate by the fault of the master or by reason of a defect in the materials supplied by him, the master shall bear the loss resulting from the destruction of the materials and is liable to the contractor for his remuneration in addition to such compensation as may be due.

When the concessionaire of the public utility service enjoys a de jure or de facto monopoly service, he is bound to observe strict equality between consumers both as regards the services rendered and the rates charged. The principle of equality does not exclude special treatment involving the reduction of remittance of rates, provided such treatment is granted to all persons who apply therefor and who fulfill the general conditions laid down by the concessionaire. 1119

Pledge of a Movable

If the thing pledged appears to be in danger of perishing, deteriorating or diminishing in value, to such an extent that there is a danger that it will not suffice to secure the claim of the pledgee, and the pledgor does not apply for the restitution of the thing in exchange for […]

### Text
If the thing pledged appears to be in danger of perishing, deteriorating or diminishing in value, to such an extent that there is a danger that it will not suffice to secure the claim of the pledgee, and the pledgor does not apply for the restitution of the thing in exchange for another thing, either the pledgee or the pledgor may apply to the Judge for authority to sell the thing pledged by public auction or at its value at the time on the stock exchange or on the market. ### Topic
Means of Payment

### Key point

### Text
A person who pays part of a debt has the right to demand a receipt for the amount he has paid and a note showing the payment on the document of title of the debt. He has also the right, at the time the debt is paid in full, to demand the restitution or cancellation of the document of title. If this document has been lost, the debtor may demand a written declaration from the creditor that the document of title has been lost. If the creditor refuses to comply with the conditions laid down in the preceding paragraph, the debtor may place the object due in judicial custody.

[EN] Give a reference card for Article 857 of the Egyptian Civil Code: the article number, the topic it falls under, and its text.

### Article Number
857

### Topic
apartments

### Key point
Every owner may, with a view to enjoying his part of the building, utilize the parts held in common, in accordance with the use for which they are intended, provided he does not prevent the other owners exercising their rights.

### Text
Every owner may, with a view to enjoying his part of the building, utilize the parts held in common, in accordance with the use for which they are intended, provided he does not prevent the other owners exercising their rights. No modification can be made to the parts held in common, even in the event of reconstruction, without the consent of all the owners, unless such modification, made by one of the owners, at his own cost, is of such a nature to facilitate the use of the parts held in common, does not change the use to which they were intended and is not prejudicial to the other owners.

[EN] Give me the English text of Article 1089 of the Egyptian Civil Code.

A creditor who wishes to obtain a judgment charge on the immovable property of his debtor must submit an application to the President of the Court of First Instance in the district in which the immovable property on which he desires to obtain the charge is situated. There's no Egyptian law that directly covers my situation. What does the judge actually look at to decide my case?

When no statutory text applies, an Egyptian judge must turn to custom first; if no custom applies, to the principles of Islamic Sharia; and in their absence, to the principles of natural justice and the rules of equity. That hierarchy is set out in **Article 1 of the Egyptian Civil Code**, and it is the default fallback the courts are required to follow whenever the codified law is silent.

I'm advising a client whose dispute has no direct statutory provision in the Civil Code. What is the proper legal hierarchy my pleadings should rely on?

The applicable hierarchy is fixed by **Article 1 of the Egyptian Civil Code**: in the absence of an applicable statutory provision, the court applies custom; in the absence of custom, the principles of Islamic Sharia; and in their absence, the principles of natural justice and the rules of equity. Your pleadings should (i) establish on the record that the codified text is silent on the precise question, (ii) move under the next applicable source in that hierarchy, and (iii) adduce evidence of the relevant custom or principle relied upon.

الترتيب الواجب التطبيق محدد بـ**المادة 1 من القانون المدني المصري**: في غياب النص التشريعي المنطبق، يحكم القاضي بمقتضى العرف، فإن لم يوجد فبمبادئ الشريعة الإسلامية، فإن لم توجد فبمبادئ القانون الطبيعي وقواعد العدالة. يُستحسن في المذكرة (1) إثبات سكوت النص عن المسألة محل النزاع، (2) تأسيس الطلبات على المصدر التالي في الترتيب، (3) تقديم ما يثبت العرف أو المبدأ المُستند إليه.
An old law I rely on seems contradicted by a newer one. How do I know if the older one is still valid or has been repealed?

A statutory provision can only be repealed in three ways under **Article 2 of the Egyptian Civil Code**: by a subsequent law that expressly says it is repealed, by a subsequent law containing a provision incompatible with the older one, or by a subsequent law that re-regulates the same subject from scratch. If none of these has happened, the older provision is still in force; if any of them has, the newer law overrides it on the conflicting points.
في قانون قديم بعتمد عليه بس فيه قانون جديد يبان متعارض معاه. أعرف إزاي إذا كان القديم لسه شغال ولا اتلغى؟

**المادة 2 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن النص التشريعي ميتلغيش إلا بتلات طرق: نص لاحق يقول صراحة إنه ملغي، أو نص لاحق فيه حكم يتعارض مع القديم، أو نص لاحق ينظم نفس الموضوع من جديد. لو محصلش حاجة من دول، النص القديم لسه شغال؛ لو حصلت واحدة، النص الجديد بيغلب على نقاط التعارض.
I need to determine whether a former statutory provision has been impliedly repealed by subsequent legislation that does not contain an express repeal clause. What legal test applies?

**Article 2 of the Egyptian Civil Code** governs. Repeal occurs in three circumstances: (i) express repeal in the subsequent law, (ii) a provision in the subsequent law incompatible with the former provision, or (iii) the subsequent law re-regulating ab novo the matter previously governed. For implied repeal you must establish either substantive incompatibility on the specific point or comprehensive re-regulation of the subject-matter. Mere overlap or coexistence is not sufficient; partial inconsistency triggers only partial repeal on the conflicting issue.
محتاج أحدد إذا كان نص تشريعي قديم اتلغى ضمنًا بتشريع لاحق مفيهوش إلغاء صريح. إيه المعيار القانوني المطبق؟

تحكم **المادة 2 من القانون المدني المصري** هذه المسألة. الإلغاء يقع في ثلاث حالات: (1) الإلغاء الصريح في النص اللاحق، (2) ورود نص في التشريع اللاحق يتعارض مع النص القديم، (3) إعادة تنظيم الموضوع الذي سبق أن قرر قواعده النص القديم. لإثبات الإلغاء الضمني يلزم إثبات التعارض الموضوعي على النقطة محل النزاع أو إعادة التنظيم الشامل للموضوع. مجرد التداخل أو التعايش لا يكفي؛ والتعارض الجزئي يؤدي إلى إلغاء جزئي فقط على النقطة المتعارضة.
My contract talks about deadlines, but I'm not sure if it uses Gregorian or Hijri dates. Which one does Egyptian law assume?

Unless the law itself explicitly says otherwise, periods are calculated using the Gregorian calendar — that's the default rule under **Article 3 of the Egyptian Civil Code**. So when your contract mentions a deadline without specifying which calendar, Egyptian law treats the period as running by Gregorian dates.
العقد بتاعي بيتكلم عن مواعيد بس مش متأكد لو هي بالميلادي ولا الهجري. القانون المصري بيفترض إيه؟

لو القانون مقالش العكس صراحة، المواعيد بتتحسب بالتقويم الميلادي — ده الأصل في **المادة 3 من القانون المدني المصري**. فلما العقد يقول معاد من غير ما يحدد التقويم، القانون المصري بيعتبر إن المدة بتجري بالميلادي.
I'm computing a limitation period that has not been expressly tied to a specific calendar by the applicable provision. Which calendar do I apply?

Apply the Gregorian calendar by default. **Article 3 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that periods of limitation are computed by the Gregorian calendar unless the law itself expressly provides otherwise. Therefore, absent an express statutory deviation specifying lunar or any other calendar, your computation should proceed by Gregorian dates.
بحسب مدة تقادم لم يربطها النص المطبق بتقويم معين. أي تقويم أعتمد؟

اعتمد التقويم الميلادي بصفة أصلية. تقرر **المادة 3 من القانون المدني المصري** أن المواعيد تحسب بالتقويم الميلادي ما لم ينص القانون على غير ذلك صراحة. وعليه، في غياب نص خاص يحدد تقويمًا آخر، يتم الحساب وفق التقويم الميلادي.
I used my legal right normally and it accidentally caused someone else a loss. Can they still sue me for damages?

No — as long as your exercise of the right was legitimate, you are not liable for resulting harm. **Article 4 of the Egyptian Civil Code** explicitly protects people who exercise their rights lawfully from being held responsible for any prejudice that arises from that lawful exercise. The defense fails only if the right was abused, but plain legitimate use is fully protected.
أنا استعملت حقي بشكل عادي وصدفة ده سبب ضرر لحد. ينفع يقاضيني ويطلب تعويض؟

لأ — طالما استعمال الحق كان مشروع، انت مش مسؤول عن الضرر اللي حصل. **المادة 4 من القانون المدني المصري** بتحمي صراحة اللي بيستعمل حقه بشكل مشروع من أي مسؤولية عن الضرر اللي بيترتب على الاستعمال ده. الحماية بتسقط بس لو تعسف في استعمال الحق، أما الاستعمال المشروع العادي محمي بالكامل.
I'm defending a client who legitimately exercised a right and incidental harm arose. What is the primary substantive defense?

Plead the principle codified in **Article 4 of the Egyptian Civil Code**: a person who exercises his right legitimately is not responsible for any prejudice resulting therefrom. The defense requires you to establish (i) the existence of the right invoked, (ii) that its exercise fell within the bounds of legitimacy, and (iii) that the harm was a consequence of that lawful exercise rather than of an abusive act. If the plaintiff alleges abuse of right under Article 5, the burden shifts to them on the elements of abuse.
بدافع عن موكلي اللي استعمل حقه استعمال مشروع ونشأ عن ذلك ضرر عرضي للغير. ما هو الدفع الموضوعي الأساسي؟

ادفع بالمبدأ المقرر في **المادة 4 من القانون المدني المصري**: من استعمل حقه استعمالًا مشروعًا لا يكون مسؤولًا عما ينشأ عن ذلك من ضرر. الدفع يستلزم إثبات (1) وجود الحق المتمسك به، (2) أن استعماله جاء في حدود المشروعية، (3) أن الضرر نتج عن هذا الاستعمال المشروع لا عن تصرف تعسفي. وإذا ادعى المدعي التعسف وفقًا للمادة 5، انتقل عبء الإثبات إليه في عناصر التعسف.
My neighbor keeps doing things on his property that are clearly meant only to annoy me — the harm to me is huge but he gets almost nothing out of it. Can he still hide behind 'it's my right'?

No. **Article 5 of the Egyptian Civil Code** treats the exercise of a right as unlawful in three cases: (i) when the sole purpose is to harm someone else, (ii) when the benefit gained is disproportionately small compared with the harm caused, or (iii) when the interest pursued is itself unlawful. Your neighbour's defense of 'lawful use of my right' fails on any of those grounds — and Article 5 gives you the basis to claim cessation of the act and compensation for the harm.
جاري بيعمل تصرفات على ملكه واضح إنها بس عشان يضايقني، الضرر اللي بيلحقني كبير جدًا والفايدة اللي بترجع عليه تقريبا صفر. ينفع يستخبى ورا 'ده حقي'؟

لأ. **المادة 5 من القانون المدني المصري** بتعتبر استعمال الحق غير مشروع في تلات حالات: (1) لو القصد منه مجرد الإضرار بالغير، (2) لو المصلحة منه قليلة جدًا مقارنة بالضرر اللي بيتسبب فيه، (3) لو المصلحة نفسها غير مشروعة. دفاع جارك بإن 'ده حقي' بيسقط لو واحدة منهم اتحققت — والمادة 5 بتديك أساس قانوني تطلب وقف التصرف والتعويض عن الضرر.

I'm representing a client who suffered substantial harm from a neighbor's repeated acts on his own property. The neighbor pleads lawful exercise of his ownership right. On what doctrine can I attack that defense?

The defense of lawful exercise of right is overcome by establishing abuse of right under **Article 5 of the Egyptian Civil Code**. Article 5 deems the act unlawful in three alternative cases: (i) it was done with the sole purpose of harming the plaintiff; (ii) the interest the defendant pursues is of disproportionately minor importance compared with the harm sustained; or (iii) the interest pursued is itself unlawful. Establishing any one suffices. The evidentiary focus is the defendant's purpose and the proportionality between the benefit and the harm.
موكلي اتضرر من تصرفات متكررة من جاره على ملكه. الجار بيتمسك بمشروعية استعمال حقه في الملكية. أهاجم الدفع ده بأي أساس؟

يُهدم الدفع باستعمال الحق المشروع بإثبات التعسف فيه استنادًا إلى **المادة 5 من القانون المدني المصري**. تعتبر المادة 5 التصرف غير مشروع في إحدى ثلاث حالات بديلة: (1) إذا لم يُقصد به سوى الإضرار بالغير؛ (2) إذا كانت المصلحة التي يبتغيها صاحب الحق قليلة الأهمية إلى حد لا يتناسب مع الضرر الواقع؛ (3) إذا كانت المصلحة التي يهدف إلى تحقيقها غير مشروعة. تكفي واحدة منها. عبء الإثبات يتمحور حول قصد المُتعسِف وعلاقة التناسب بين المصلحة والضرر.
A new law just changed who counts as legally capable. I made a contract before it took effect — does that contract become invalid now?

No. Under **Article 6 of the Egyptian Civil Code**, when a new law makes a person legally incapable who was capable under the old law, that new incapacity does not retroactively affect acts they validly performed before the new law came into force. Your prior contract stays valid; only acts done after the new law takes effect would be governed by the new capacity rules.
في قانون جديد طلع غير اللي ينفع يتصرف قانوني. أنا عملت عقد قبل ما القانون يطلع — هل العقد يبقى باطل دلوقتي؟

لأ. **المادة 6 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن لو القانون الجديد عمل شخص ناقص الأهلية وكان كامل الأهلية بالقانون القديم، النقص ده ميأثرش على تصرفاته اللي عملها قبل القانون الجديد. عقدك القديم يفضل صحيح؛ بس التصرفات بعد سريان القانون الجديد هي اللي تخضع للقواعد الجديدة.
A new statute alters the criteria for legal capacity. I need to advise on the validity of acts my client performed before the new statute came into force.

Such pre-existing acts are protected. **Article 6 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that where a person was legally capable under former provisions and becomes incapable under new ones, the new incapacity does not affect the validity of acts previously done. Your client's prior acts remain valid; only post-enactment acts are governed by the new capacity criteria. The first paragraph of Article 6 also clarifies that capacity provisions apply to all persons who meet the conditions they set.
تشريع جديد يغير معايير الأهلية. أحتاج إفادة بصحة تصرفات أجراها موكلي قبل سريان التشريع الجديد.

هذه التصرفات السابقة محمية. **المادة 6 من القانون المدني المصري** تقرر أنه إذا كان الشخص كامل الأهلية وفق النصوص القديمة وأصبح ناقص الأهلية وفق النصوص الجديدة، فإن ذلك لا يؤثر في صحة تصرفاته السابقة. تصرفات موكلك القديمة تبقى صحيحة؛ وتخضع التصرفات اللاحقة فقط للمعايير الجديدة. كما توضح الفقرة الأولى من المادة 6 أن النصوص المتعلقة بالأهلية تسري على جميع الأشخاص الذين تتوافر فيهم شروطها.
A new law just changed how long I have to file my case. My time was already running under the old law — which one applies now?

From the moment the new law comes into force, it applies to every prescription period that hasn't yet been completed. **Article 7 of the Egyptian Civil Code** sets this rule, but it carves out an important exception: the old law still governs when the period started, and any suspension or interruption that happened before the new law came into force. So the running clock follows the new rules going forward, but how the clock began and any pauses before the change are judged by the old law.
في قانون جديد غير المدة اللي عندي عشان أرفع قضيتي. المدة كانت بتجري بالقانون القديم — أمشي على إيه دلوقتي؟

من ساعة ما القانون الجديد يبدأ يسري، بيطبَّق على كل تقادم لسه ميكتملش. ده اللي بتقوله **المادة 7 من القانون المدني المصري**، بس مع استثناء مهم: القانون القديم يفضل هو المرجع في تحديد بداية المدة وأي وقف أو انقطاع حصل قبل الجديد. يعني عقارب الساعة بتمشي بالقانون الجديد من هنا ورايح، إنما البداية والوقفات السابقة بتتحسب بالقديم.
Legislation enacted during a running limitation period altered the rules. I need to determine which law governs continuation, commencement, suspension, and interruption.

**Article 7 of the Egyptian Civil Code** splits the analysis: (i) new provisions on prescription apply prospectively to all running periods not yet completed; (ii) former provisions, however, continue to govern commencement, suspension, and interruption insofar as those events fall within the period preceding the new law's effective date. In practice, you compute the running period under the new rules from the effective date forward, but you locate the dies a quo, and assess any pre-effective-date suspensions or interruptions, under the former law.
صدر تشريع أثناء جريان مدة التقادم وعدّل القواعد. أحتاج تحديد القانون الواجب التطبيق على الجريان والبدء والوقف والانقطاع.

**المادة 7 من القانون المدني المصري** تقسم التحليل: (1) النصوص الجديدة المتعلقة بالتقادم تسري بأثر مباشر على كل تقادم لم يكتمل من وقت العمل بها؛ (2) أما النصوص القديمة، فتظل سارية على المسائل الخاصة ببدء التقادم ووقفه وانقطاعه عن المدة السابقة على العمل بالنصوص الجديدة. عمليًا: تحسب جريان المدة بالقواعد الجديدة من تاريخ نفاذها، وتحدد نقطة البدء وتُقيّم أي وقف أو انقطاع سابق على نفاذ الجديد بالقواعد القديمة.
The new law shortened the time I have to bring my case. Does my old, longer period still apply, or does the new shorter one kick in?

If the new law provides a shorter prescription period, the new shorter period applies and starts running from the day the new law came into force — even if your time had already begun under the old law. There's one exception under **Article 8 of the Egyptian Civil Code**: if the remaining time left under the old law is even shorter than the new period, your prescription completes on that earlier old-law expiry date. So you get whichever is shorter — and the law won't surprise you with a longer-than-expected deadline.
القانون الجديد قصّر المدة اللي ينفع فيها أرفع قضيتي. المدة القديمة الطويلة لسه شغالة، ولا الجديدة القصيرة هي اللي بتسري؟

لو القانون الجديد قرر مدة تقادم أقصر، المدة الجديدة هي اللي تسري وبتبدأ من تاريخ العمل بالقانون الجديد، حتى لو المدة القديمة كانت قد بدأت قبل كده. بس فيه استثناء في **المادة 8 من القانون المدني المصري**: لو الباقي من المدة القديمة أقصر من المدة الجديدة، التقادم يتم بانتهاء الباقي ده. يعني بتاخد الأقصر بين الاتنين، والقانون مش هيفاجئك بمدة أطول من اللي مفروض.
Subsequent legislation has shortened the prescription period applicable to my client's claim. The old period had already started running. How do I compute the deadline?

**Article 8 of the Egyptian Civil Code** prescribes the method. The new, shorter period applies from the effective date of the new law, even where the old period had already commenced — but if the unexpired remainder under the former law is shorter than the new statutory period, prescription completes upon the exhaustion of that remainder. Operationally: compute the new-period end-date measured from the new law's effective date, compute the old-period end-date measured from its original dies a quo, and the prescription expires on the earlier of the two.
صدر تشريع لاحق يقصّر مدة التقادم المنطبقة على دعوى موكلي. المدة القديمة كانت قد بدأت بالفعل. كيف أحسب الميعاد؟

تحدد **المادة 8 من القانون المدني المصري** الطريقة. المدة الجديدة الأقصر تسري من تاريخ العمل بالقانون الجديد ولو كانت المدة القديمة قد بدأت — ولكن إذا كان الباقي من المدة القديمة أقصر من المدة الجديدة، فإن التقادم يتم بانقضاء هذا الباقي. عمليًا: احسب نهاية المدة الجديدة من تاريخ نفاذ القانون الجديد، واحسب نهاية المدة القديمة من تاريخ بدئها الأصلي، وينقضي الحق بانتهاء أيهما يحل أولًا.
I prepared some evidence years ago for a future dispute. Now the law about proof has changed — which version applies to my old evidence?

Evidence that you prepared in advance is governed by the law in force at the time you prepared it (or at the time when it should have been prepared). That's the rule in **Article 9 of the Egyptian Civil Code**. So your old evidence is judged by the old proof rules — a later change to the law on proof does not retroactively invalidate or alter how your pre-prepared evidence is assessed.
حضّرت دلائل من سنين علشان نزاع محتمل. دلوقتي قواعد الإثبات اتغيرت — إيه اللي يطبَّق على دلائلي القديمة؟

الأدلة اللي بتتعد مقدماً بتخضع للنصوص اللي كانت سارية وقت ما اتعدت (أو وقت ما المفروض اتعدت فيه). ده اللي بتقرره **المادة 9 من القانون المدني المصري**. يعني دلائلك القديمة بتتقيَّم بقواعد الإثبات اللي كانت موجودة وقتها، والقانون الجديد ميأثرش بأثر رجعي على تقييم الدلائل المُعَدّة مسبقًا.
Proof was established in advance under the prior legal regime; the rules of evidence have since changed. Which regime governs admissibility and probative weight?

**Article 9 of the Egyptian Civil Code** assigns governance to the law in force at the time the proof was established, or at the time when such proof should have been established. The temporal anchor is the moment of establishment, not the moment of litigation. Subsequent statutory changes to the rules of proof do not retroactively govern pre-existing pre-constituted evidence; admissibility and probative analysis proceed under the regime contemporaneous with the establishment of the proof.
أُعدّت أدلة مقدمًا في ظل النظام القانوني السابق ثم تغيرت قواعد الإثبات. أي قانون يحكم القبول والقوة الإثباتية؟

تسند **المادة 9 من القانون المدني المصري** الحكم إلى النصوص المعمول بها في الوقت الذي تم فيه إعداد الدليل، أو في الوقت الذي كان ينبغي إعداده فيه. النقطة الزمنية المرجعية هي لحظة الإعداد، لا لحظة التقاضي. والتعديلات اللاحقة لا تحكم بأثر رجعي الأدلة المُعَدّة مسبقًا؛ فيُقيَّم القبول والقوة الإثباتية في ضوء القانون المعاصر لإعداد الدليل.
I have a contract with a foreign company. There's a dispute about which country's law applies. Who decides what type of relationship this even is — them or us?

Egyptian law decides. **Article 10 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that when there's a conflict of laws issue, it's Egyptian law that determines the legal nature of the relationship in question — that classification then tells the court which substantive law should ultimately be applied. So before reaching the foreign law on the merits, the Egyptian court characterizes the relationship under Egyptian categories first.
عندي عقد مع شركة أجنبية وفيه نزاع على أنهي قانون اللي يطبَّق. مين اللي بيحدد نوع العلاقة دي — هم ولا إحنا؟

القانون المصري هو المرجع. **المادة 10 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن لما يبقى فيه تنازع قوانين، القانون المصري هو المرجع في تكييف نوع العلاقة — والتكييف ده هو اللي بيحدد للمحكمة القانون الموضوعي اللي ينطبق في الآخر. يعني المحكمة المصرية أول حاجة بتكيّف العلاقة بمعايير القانون المصري قبل ما تنتقل لتطبيق أي قانون أجنبي على الموضوع.
I'm litigating a private-international-law dispute in Egyptian courts and a preliminary question of characterization (qualification) has arisen. Whose conflicts categories control?

Egyptian law controls characterization. **Article 10 of the Egyptian Civil Code** establishes that Egyptian law is the reference point for determining the nature of a legal relationship when classification is required to identify the law applicable in a conflict-of-laws case. Functionally, the lex fori (Egyptian law) governs the qualification step; only after the relationship has been characterized under Egyptian categories does the court apply the choice-of-law rule and reach the foreign substantive law that ultimately governs the issue.
أرافع في نزاع تنازع قوانين أمام المحاكم المصرية وأُثيرت مسألة أولية بشأن التكييف. أي قانون يحكم التكييف؟

القانون المصري يحكم التكييف. تقرر **المادة 10 من القانون المدني المصري** أن القانون المصري هو المرجع في تكييف العلاقات عندما يطلب تحديد نوعها في قضية يتنازع فيها القوانين لمعرفة القانون الواجب التطبيق. وظيفيًا: قانون القاضي (المصري) يحكم خطوة التكييف؛ ثم بعد تكييف العلاقة وفق المعايير المصرية تطبق المحكمة قاعدة الإسناد وتصل إلى القانون الموضوعي الأجنبي الذي يحكم المسألة.
I signed a deal in Egypt with a foreign person who later claimed he lacked legal capacity under his own country's law. Can he get out of the deal that easily?

Probably not. The general rule under **Article 11 of the Egyptian Civil Code** is that a person's legal capacity is governed by the law of their nationality — but there's a strong protective exception for transactions concluded and taking effect in Egypt: if the foreigner's incapacity is due to a non-apparent reason that the other party couldn't easily detect, that reason has no effect on his capacity for that Egyptian transaction. So if his lack of capacity wasn't reasonably discoverable, he can't use it to escape your contract.
أنا وقعت صفقة في مصر مع شخص أجنبي وبعدين قال إنه ناقص الأهلية حسب قانون بلده. ينفع يخرج من الصفقة كده ببساطة؟

غالبًا لأ. الأصل في **المادة 11 من القانون المدني المصري** إن أهلية الشخص تحكمها جنسيته — بس فيه استثناء قوي بيحمي الصفقات اللي بتتم وتسري آثارها في مصر: لو نقص الأهلية بتاع الأجنبي راجع لسبب فيه خفاء ومش سهل الطرف التاني يلاحظه، السبب ده ميأثرش على أهليته في الصفقة المصرية دي. فلو نقص الأهلية ميقدرش الواحد يكتشفه بسهولة، الراجل ميقدرش يستخدمه يهرب من العقد.
A foreign individual party to a pecuniary transaction concluded in Egypt asserts incapacity under his lex patriae. The other party is Egyptian. What is the result?

**Article 11 of the Egyptian Civil Code** governs. The status and legal capacity of persons are in principle governed by the law of nationality. However, where the transaction is pecuniary, concluded in Egypt, and producing effects in Egypt, and where the foreigner's incapacity is due to a cause that is not apparent and which the other party could not easily have detected, the incapacity has no effect on his capacity for that transaction. The Egyptian counterparty's good-faith ignorance of the latent incapacity neutralises the lex patriae rule for the protective purpose of intra-Egyptian commercial security. The same article also provides that foreign juristic persons are governed by the law of their actual principal place of management, except that Egyptian law applies if their principal activity is in Egypt.
طرف أجنبي في معاملة مالية أُبرمت في مصر يدفع بنقص الأهلية وفقًا لقانونه الوطني. الطرف الآخر مصري. ما الحكم؟

تحكم **المادة 11 من القانون المدني المصري**. الأصل أن الحالة المدنية والأهلية تخضع لقانون الجنسية. ومع ذلك، ففي التصرفات المالية التي تعقد في مصر وتترتب آثارها فيها، إذا كان نقص الأهلية يرجع إلى سبب فيه خفاء لا يسهل على الطرف الآخر تبيُّنه، فإن هذا السبب لا يؤثر في أهليته في تلك المعاملة. حسن نية المتعاقد المصري في جهله بنقص الأهلية الخفي يحيّد قاعدة قانون الجنسية حماية لاستقرار المعاملات الداخلية. وتقرر المادة 11 كذلك أن الأشخاص الاعتبارية الأجنبية يحكمها قانون مركز الإدارة الرئيسي الفعلي، إلا إذا باشرت نشاطها الرئيسي في مصر فيسري القانون المصري.
I'm planning to marry someone of a different nationality. Which country's law decides whether the marriage is even valid?

Each spouse's home-country law applies to the substantive conditions of validity for that spouse. Under **Article 12 of the Egyptian Civil Code**, the fundamental conditions for a valid marriage are governed by the national law of each of the two future spouses — so your validity is judged by your national law and your partner's by theirs. Both sets of conditions must be satisfied for the marriage to be substantively valid.
ناوي أتجوز شخص من جنسية تانية. أنهي قانون اللي بيقرر إذا كان الجواز ده صحيح أصلًا؟

كل واحد فيكم بيتطبق عليه قانون جنسيته بالنسبة لشروط صحة الزواج الموضوعية. **المادة 12 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن الشروط الموضوعية لصحة الزواج يرجع فيها لقانون كل من الزوجين — يعني صحتك بتتحدد بقانون جنسيتك، وصحته بتتحدد بقانون جنسيته. ولازم الاتنين تتوافروا في وقت واحد علشان الزواج يكون صحيح موضوعيًا.
I'm advising on a prospective Egyptian-foreign marriage. Which law governs the substantive conditions of validity?

**Article 12 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that the fundamental conditions relating to the validity of marriage are governed by the national law of each of the two spouses. Each spouse's substantive capacity to marry, impediments, and other validity requirements are tested under their own lex patriae — both sets must be satisfied. Formal validity is governed by other choice-of-law rules; substantive impediments under each national law (e.g., kinship, prior bond, statutory minimum) must each be individually cleared. Article 14 should also be considered if one spouse is Egyptian at the time of the marriage.
أستشار في زواج مرتقب بين مصري وأجنبي. أي قانون يحكم الشروط الموضوعية للصحة؟

تقرر **المادة 12 من القانون المدني المصري** أن الشروط الموضوعية لصحة الزواج يرجع فيها إلى قانون كل من الزوجين. أهلية الزواج الموضوعية والموانع وسائر شروط الصحة تُختبر لكل زوج وفق قانون جنسيته — ويلزم استيفاء كلتا المنظومتين. أما الصحة الشكلية فتحكمها قواعد إسناد أخرى. كل مانع موضوعي في كل قانون وطني (كالقرابة أو الزواج القائم أو السن الأدنى) يجب اجتيازه بصورة مستقلة. وينبغي مراعاة المادة 14 إذا كان أحد الزوجين مصريًا وقت انعقاد الزواج.
I'm in a cross-border marriage and we're discussing separation. Which country's law decides how it ends — his country or mine?

Under **Article 13 of the Egyptian Civil Code**, the effects of the marriage (including effects on property) are governed by the law of the country to which the husband belongs at the time of conclusion of the marriage. For repudiation, it's the husband's national law at the time of repudiation. For divorce and judicial separation, it's the husband's national law at the time legal proceedings start. So the husband's nationality controls — but the relevant moment depends on which type of termination is at issue.
أنا في زواج بين جنسيتين مختلفتين، وبنفكر في الانفصال. قانون بلد مين بيحدد إزاي بيخلص — بلده ولا بلدي؟

حسب **المادة 13 من القانون المدني المصري**: آثار الزواج (بما فيها الآثار على المال) يحكمها قانون بلد الزوج وقت انعقاد الزواج. الطلاق (التطليق من جانب الزوج) يحكمه قانون بلد الزوج وقت إيقاع الطلاق. التطليق القضائي والانفصال يحكمهم قانون بلد الزوج وقت بدء الدعوى. يعني جنسية الزوج هي اللي بتحكم، بس النقطة الزمنية بتختلف حسب نوع إنهاء العلاقة.
I'm advising on the choice-of-law analysis for spousal effects, repudiation, and divorce in a cross-border marriage.

Apply **Article 13 of the Egyptian Civil Code**: the effects of the marriage, including its effects upon the property of the spouses, are governed by the law of the husband's nationality at the time of conclusion of the marriage. Repudiation is governed by the husband's national law at the time of repudiation. Divorce and judicial separation are governed by the husband's national law at the time the legal proceedings commence. The connecting factor is uniformly the husband's nationality, but the temporal anchor varies by category: contract-conclusion for effects, repudiation-act for repudiation, and litis-commencement for divorce/separation. Article 14 must be considered if either spouse is Egyptian at marriage.
أستشار في تحديد القانون الواجب التطبيق على آثار الزواج والطلاق والتطليق في زواج بين جنسيتين.

طبّق **المادة 13 من القانون المدني المصري**: يسري على آثار الزواج، بما فيها الأثر بالنسبة إلى مال الزوجين، قانون بلد الزوج وقت انعقاد الزواج. ويسري على الطلاق قانون بلد الزوج وقت الطلاق. ويسري على التطليق والانفصال قانون بلد الزوج وقت رفع الدعوى. ضابط الإسناد ثابت في جنسية الزوج، لكن النقطة الزمنية تتغير: لحظة الانعقاد للآثار، ولحظة الطلاق للطلاق، ولحظة بدء الدعوى للتطليق والانفصال. وتلزم مراعاة المادة 14 إذا كان أحد الزوجين مصريًا وقت الزواج.
My husband is Egyptian, I'm a foreign national, and we married while he held Egyptian nationality. Which country's law applies to our divorce now?

Egyptian law applies — and only Egyptian law — to almost every issue. **Article 14 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that in the cases covered by Articles 12 and 13 (marriage effects, repudiation, divorce, separation), where one of the spouses was Egyptian at the time of the marriage, Egyptian law alone governs. The one carve-out is the spouses' legal capacity to marry, which remains under their respective national laws. So your divorce proceeds under Egyptian rules.
جوزي مصري وأنا جنسية تانية، واتجوزنا وهو على جنسيته المصرية. قانون بلد مين بيطبَّق على الطلاق دلوقتي؟

بيتطبق القانون المصري — وبس — على أغلب المسائل. **المادة 14 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن في الأحوال اللي بتغطيها المادتين 12 و13 (آثار الزواج، الطلاق، التطليق، الانفصال)، لو أحد الزوجين كان مصري وقت انعقاد الزواج، يسري القانون المصري وحده. والاستثناء الوحيد بتاع المادة 14 هو شرط الأهلية للزواج، اللي يفضل بيتطبق فيه قانون جنسية كل واحد. فطلاقك بيمشي بالقواعد المصرية.
In a mixed-nationality marriage where one spouse held Egyptian nationality at the time of marriage, what is the choice-of-law for marriage effects, divorce, and separation?

**Article 14 of the Egyptian Civil Code** displaces the connecting factors of Articles 12 and 13 in this situation: where one spouse is Egyptian at the time of conclusion of the marriage, Egyptian law alone applies — with the express exception of the legal capacity to marry, which remains governed by the respective national laws under Article 12. The exception is narrowly construed; substantive marriage effects, property consequences, repudiation, divorce, and judicial separation are governed exclusively by Egyptian substantive law.
في زواج مختلط الجنسية كان أحد الزوجين فيه مصريًا وقت الزواج، ما القانون الواجب التطبيق على آثار الزواج والطلاق والتطليق؟

تعطّل **المادة 14 من القانون المدني المصري** ضوابط الإسناد المقررة في المادتين 12 و13 في هذه الحالة: إذا كان أحد الزوجين مصريًا وقت انعقاد الزواج، يسري القانون المصري وحده، باستثناء صريح يخص شرط الأهلية للزواج الذي يظل خاضعًا لقانون كل من الزوجين بمقتضى المادة 12. وهذا الاستثناء يفسَّر تفسيرًا ضيقًا؛ فآثار الزواج الموضوعية والمالية والطلاق والتطليق والانفصال جميعًا تخضع للقانون المصري الموضوعي وحده.
My relative who lives abroad owes me support. Which country's law decides how much and whether they actually owe it?

It's the national law of the person who has to pay. **Article 15 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that the obligation to pay alimony between relatives is governed by the national law of the person liable for the payment — not the law of the recipient or the country where either of you lives. So whether the duty exists, who has to pay, and how much, are all tested under the law of the debtor's nationality.
قريبي اللي ساكن برة بيدفعلي نفقة. قانون بلد مين هو اللي بيحدد قد إيه وإذا كان فعلًا ملزَم يدفعها؟

قانون جنسية اللي عليه الدفع. **المادة 15 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن الالتزام بالنفقة بين الأقارب يحكمه قانون المدين بها — مش قانون اللي بياخدها ولا قانون البلد اللي عايشين فيها. يعني وجود الالتزام، ومين عليه الدفع، وقد إيه، كل ده بيتحدد بقانون جنسية الشخص اللي عليه الدفع.
Which national law governs an alimony obligation between relatives in a cross-border setting?

**Article 15 of the Egyptian Civil Code** designates the law of the nationality of the obligor — the person liable for the alimony payment. That law governs the existence, scope, and amount of the obligation. The recipient's nationality, residence, and the place of intended payment are irrelevant to the choice-of-law step; the dispositive connecting factor is the debtor's lex patriae.
أي قانون وطني يحكم التزامًا بالنفقة بين الأقارب في نزاع عابر للحدود؟

تسند **المادة 15 من القانون المدني المصري** الاختصاص إلى قانون جنسية المدين بالنفقة. هذا القانون يحكم وجود الالتزام ونطاقه ومقداره. أما جنسية المنتفع وإقامته ومكان الوفاء المتوقع فلا أثر لها على خطوة تحديد القانون الواجب التطبيق؛ والضابط الحاسم هو قانون جنسية المدين.
My elderly father (a foreign national) needs a guardian arranged. Which country's law decides who can be guardian and what the rules are?

The national law of the person being protected applies. **Article 16 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that the substantive rules on guardianship, trusteeship, receivership, and other systems of protection for those without legal capacity or for absent persons are governed by the national law of the person who needs protection — your father in this case. So the substantive framework follows his nationality, not yours and not the country where the proceedings are conducted.
أبويا (جنسية أجنبية) كبر سنه ومحتاج وصي. قانون بلد مين بيحدد مين يبقى الوصي وإيه القواعد؟

قانون جنسية الشخص اللي محتاج حماية. **المادة 16 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن المسائل الموضوعية الخاصة بالولاية والوصاية والقوامة وأنظمة حماية المحجور عليهم والغائبين يحكمها قانون الشخص اللي بتجب حمايته — أبوك في الحالة دي. يعني القواعد الموضوعية بتمشي على جنسيته هو، مش جنسيتك ولا بلد رفع الدعوى.
I'm advising on the choice-of-law for guardianship of a foreign national lacking capacity in Egypt.

**Article 16 of the Egyptian Civil Code** designates the connecting factor as the national law of the person who must be protected. That law governs the substantive aspects of natural and legal guardianship, trusteeship, receivership, and other protective systems applicable to those without legal capacity and to absent persons. The Egyptian court has jurisdiction and may apply procedural law lex fori, but the substantive content — appointment criteria, powers, accountability, removal — is referred to the protected person's lex patriae.
أستشار في القانون الواجب التطبيق على وصاية أجنبي ناقص الأهلية في مصر.

تحدد **المادة 16 من القانون المدني المصري** ضابط الإسناد بقانون جنسية الشخص الذي تجب حمايته. يحكم هذا القانون المسائل الموضوعية للولاية والوصاية والقوامة وسائر نظم حماية المحجور عليهم والغائبين. للمحكمة المصرية الاختصاص وقد تطبق قانون القاضي إجرائيًا، لكن الموضوع — معايير التعيين والسلطات والمساءلة والعزل — يحال إلى قانون جنسية الشخص محل الحماية.
My uncle who lived abroad just passed away. He left a will. Which country's law decides what happens to his estate?

It depends on what part of the question you're asking. **Article 17 of the Egyptian Civil Code** distinguishes substance from form: the substance of inheritance, wills, and other dispositions taking effect after death is governed by the national law of the deceased at the time of his death. But the form of a will is governed either by the testator's national law at the time the will was made, OR by the law of the country where the will was made — whichever validly covers it. So substance follows his nationality; form has the extra fallback of the place of execution.
عمي اللي كان ساكن برة توفى وساب وصية. قانون بلد مين بيحدد إيه اللي يحصل في تركته؟

بيعتمد على الجزء اللي بتسأل عنه. **المادة 17 من القانون المدني المصري** بتفرق بين الموضوع والشكل: موضوع الميراث والوصية وأي تصرفات مضافة لما بعد الموت يحكمها قانون جنسية المورث (أو الموصي) وقت موته. لكن شكل الوصية يحكمه قانون الموصي وقت ما كتب الوصية، أو قانون البلد اللي اتعملت فيه الوصية — أي واحد فيهم يصححها. يعني الموضوع بيمشي على جنسيته، والشكل عنده مرجع إضافي وهو مكان تحرير الوصية.
I need to determine the choice-of-law for a will executed abroad by a foreign national whose estate includes Egyptian assets.

Apply **Article 17 of the Egyptian Civil Code**, which bifurcates: (i) the substance of inheritance, wills, and other mortis causa dispositions is governed by the national law of the deceased / testator / disponer at the time of death; (ii) the form of the will is alternatively governed by the testator's national law at the time of execution OR by the law of the country in which the will was made — favor validitatis applies, satisfying either suffices. The same form-rule extends to other dispositions taking effect after death. Egyptian assets remain subject to procedural and public-policy controls of the forum, but the substantive choice-of-law follows the deceased's lex patriae.
أحتاج تحديد القانون الواجب التطبيق على وصية حُرّرت في الخارج من أجنبي تشمل تركته أصولًا في مصر.

طبّق **المادة 17 من القانون المدني المصري**، وهي تقسم المسألة: (1) يخضع موضوع الميراث والوصية وسائر التصرفات المضافة إلى ما بعد الموت لقانون جنسية المورث/الموصي وقت موته؛ (2) أما شكل الوصية فيخضع بصورة تخييرية لقانون الموصي وقت الإيصاء أو لقانون البلد الذي تمت فيه الوصية — وفقًا لمبدأ تفضيل الصحة يكفي توافر أحدهما. ويسري ذات حكم الشكل على سائر التصرفات المضافة إلى ما بعد الموت. تبقى الأصول المصرية خاضعة لضوابط النظام العام والإجراءات أمام محكمة القاضي، لكن الإسناد الموضوعي يتبع قانون جنسية المتوفى.
I'm signing a contract with someone living in another country. Which country's law applies if we don't write it in the contract?

If both of you share the same domicile, the law of that country applies. If you don't, it's the law of the country where you actually concluded the contract. **Article 19 of the Egyptian Civil Code** sets these defaults — but they only kick in if you didn't agree on a different law or if circumstances don't indicate another intended choice. There's also a strong special rule for immovables: any contract relating to an immovable is governed by the law of the country where the immovable is located, regardless of the other factors.
ببرم عقد مع شخص ساكن في بلد تانية. قانون بلد مين بيطبَّق لو ما كتبنهوش في العقد؟

لو موطنكوا واحد، بيطبَّق قانون البلد دي. لو موطنكوا مختلف، بيطبَّق قانون البلد اللي العقد اتم فيها. **المادة 19 من القانون المدني المصري** بتحط القواعد دي كأصل — لكنها بتطبَّق بس لو متفقتوش على قانون تاني أو الظروف ما بتشيرش لاختيار قانون مختلف. وفيه قاعدة خاصة قوية للعقارات: العقد اللي بيتعلق بعقار بيحكمه قانون موقع العقار مهما كانت العوامل التانية.
I'm drafting the choice-of-law analysis for a contract with no express choice-of-law clause and party-autonomy is in issue.

**Article 19 of the Egyptian Civil Code** sets the default cascade for contractual obligations: (i) if the parties share a common domicile, the law of that domicile applies; (ii) absent common domicile, the law of the place where the contract was concluded applies. Both defaults yield to party autonomy: they apply unless the parties agree, or the circumstances indicate that another law is intended to apply — so implied choice and tacit selection can rebut the defaults. A special rule overrides the cascade for contracts relating to immovables: the law of the situs of the immovable governs irrespective of domicile or place of conclusion.
أصوغ تحليل القانون الواجب التطبيق على عقد لا يتضمن شرط اختيار قانون صريحًا مع إثارة مبدأ سلطان الإرادة.

تضع **المادة 19 من القانون المدني المصري** السلم الافتراضي للالتزامات التعاقدية: (1) إذا اتحد موطن المتعاقدين سرى قانون الموطن المشترك؛ (2) فإن اختلف الموطن سرى قانون البلد الذي تم فيه العقد. وكلا الافتراضين يخضع لسلطان الإرادة: يطبقان ما لم يتفق المتعاقدان أو يتبين من الظروف أن قانونًا آخر هو الذي يراد تطبيقه — فيمكن للاختيار الضمني أو المستفاد من الظروف أن يدحض الافتراض. وثمة قاعدة خاصة تَجُبّ السلم في عقود العقار: يسري قانون موقع العقار على هذه العقود بصرف النظر عن الموطن أو مكان الانعقاد.
I signed a contract abroad in a way that's not standard in Egypt. Is the form acceptable for Egyptian purposes?

Likely yes, because Egyptian conflict rules give you alternatives. **Article 20 of the Egyptian Civil Code** says a contract between living persons is valid as to form if it follows the law of the country in which it was concluded — that's the primary rule. But the article also lets the form follow the law that governs the substantive provisions of the contract, or the law of the parties' domicile, or their common national law. Compliance with any of those is enough for form validity, so a contract executed abroad following local form requirements will normally be recognised.
وقعت عقد برة بشكل مش زي اللي معتاد في مصر. الشكل ده مقبول قانونيًا في مصر؟

غالبًا أيوه، لإن قواعد التنازع المصرية بتديك بدائل. **المادة 20 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن العقد بين الأحياء صحيح من حيث الشكل لو اتبع قانون البلد اللي تم فيه — وده الأصل. كمان السماح بإن الشكل يخضع لقانون الأحكام الموضوعية للعقد، أو لقانون موطن المتعاقدين، أو قانونهم الوطني المشترك. الاستيفاء لأي واحد فيهم يكفي للصحة الشكلية، فالعقد المُحرَّر برة طبقًا للشكل المحلي بيتعرف بيه عادةً.
Determine the choice-of-law applicable to the formal validity of an inter-vivos contract concluded abroad between parties with a connection to Egypt.

**Article 20 of the Egyptian Civil Code** offers alternative connecting factors for formal validity (favor validitatis): contracts between living persons are governed as to form by the law of the country of conclusion (locus regit actum) — but may alternatively be governed by the law regulating the substantive provisions of the contract, by the law of the parties' domicile, or by their common national law. Satisfying any one of these alternatives suffices for formal validity. This pluralistic approach is designed to uphold the form of cross-border instruments wherever a reasonable connecting law was followed.
حدد القانون الواجب التطبيق على الصحة الشكلية لعقد بين الأحياء أُبرم في الخارج بين أطراف لهم صلة بمصر.

تتيح **المادة 20 من القانون المدني المصري** ضوابط إسناد بديلة للصحة الشكلية تفضيلًا للصحة: العقود بين الأحياء تخضع في شكلها لقانون البلد الذي تمت فيه (locus regit actum) — ويجوز كذلك أن تخضع للقانون الذي يسري على أحكامها الموضوعية، أو لقانون موطن المتعاقدين، أو لقانونهم الوطني المشترك. ويكفي توافر أحد هذه البدائل لإقامة الصحة الشكلية. وهذا التوجه التعددي يهدف إلى الإبقاء على شكل المحررات العابرة للحدود متى استُند إلى قانون ربط معقول.
I was injured by someone abroad, and their act would have been totally legal in Egypt. Can I still sue them here under Egyptian law for it?

Probably not on that act alone. **Article 21 of the Egyptian Civil Code** says non-contractual obligations are normally governed by the law of the country where the act causing the obligation took place — but there's an important tort carve-out: an act that occurred abroad and is considered unlawful there will NOT be applied in Egypt as a tort if it is considered lawful under Egyptian law. So if the foreign act would be lawful in Egypt, Article 21 blocks importing the foreign tort claim against the actor.
اتعرضت لإصابة من حد برة، والفعل ده كان طبيعي تمامًا قانونيًا في مصر. أقدر أرفع قضية هنا بقانون مصر؟

غالبًا لأ بناءً على الفعل ده وحده. **المادة 21 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن الالتزامات غير التعاقدية بيحكمها قانون البلد اللي حصل فيه الفعل المنشئ للالتزام — بس مع استثناء مهم للفعل الضار: لو الفعل حصل برة وكان غير مشروع في البلد دي بس مشروع في مصر، الفقرة دي ما بتطبقش. يعني لو الفعل لو حصل في مصر يبقى مشروع، المادة 21 بتمنع استيراد المسؤولية التقصيرية الأجنبية ضد الفاعل.
I'm assessing tortious choice-of-law for an act that occurred abroad but whose legal characterization differs between the foreign lex loci delicti and Egyptian law.

**Article 21 of the Egyptian Civil Code** governs. The general rule for non-contractual obligations is lex loci actus — the law of the place where the act giving rise to the obligation occurred. However, paragraph 2 of Article 21 carves out tort: the lex loci does not apply to acts that occurred abroad and are considered unlawful by that foreign law but lawful in Egypt. The dual-illegality requirement protects Egyptian conceptions of lawfulness; if either limb fails (lawful abroad or unlawful in Egypt), the analysis proceeds as Article 21 prescribes.
أقيّم تحديد القانون الواجب التطبيق على فعل ضار وقع في الخارج ويختلف وصفه القانوني بين قانون محل وقوع الفعل والقانون المصري.

تحكم **المادة 21 من القانون المدني المصري**. القاعدة العامة للالتزامات غير التعاقدية هي قانون محل الفعل: قانون البلد الذي وقع فيه الفعل المنشئ للالتزام. غير أن الفقرة الثانية تستثني الفعل الضار: لا تسري أحكام الفقرة الأولى على الوقائع التي تحدث في الخارج وتكون مشروعة في مصر وإن كانت تعد غير مشروعة في البلد الذي وقعت فيه. اشتراط ازدواج عدم المشروعية يحمي مفاهيم المشروعية في القانون المصري؛ فإن سقط أحد الطرفين سرى ما تقرره المادة 21.
I'm involved in a lawsuit in Egypt with foreign parties. Which country's procedural rules apply to the case?

Egyptian rules. **Article 22 of the Egyptian Civil Code** provides that competence of courts and all questions of procedure are governed by the law of the country where the action is brought or the proceedings are conducted. So in an Egyptian forum, Egyptian procedural law applies to the proceedings — even if the substantive merits ultimately turn on foreign law.
في قضية في مصر مع أطراف أجانب. قواعد المرافعات بتاعة بلد مين هي اللي تطبَّق على القضية؟

القواعد المصرية. **المادة 22 من القانون المدني المصري** بتقول إن قواعد الاختصاص وجميع المسائل الخاصة بالإجراءات يحكمها قانون البلد اللي بتُقام فيه الدعوى أو بتُباشر فيه الإجراءات. يعني في المحكمة المصرية بيتطبق قانون المرافعات المصري على الإجراءات — حتى لو الموضوع نفسه في النهاية بيتحكمه قانون أجنبي.
Determine the choice-of-law for procedural and jurisdictional questions in a cross-border matter pending before Egyptian courts.

**Article 22 of the Egyptian Civil Code** designates lex fori. Principles of competence (jurisdiction) and all questions of procedure are governed by the law of the country in which the action is brought or in which the proceedings are taken. The procedural/substantive boundary is therefore drawn under the lex fori for the procedural side, while substantive entitlements remain subject to the relevant connecting rules of Articles 11–21 et seq.
